Proposition
[Homology of a point] 1. ch2:2.8\group Singular Homology

For a point, $H_0\cong \mathbb {Z}$ and $H_n=0$ for $n>0$.
Proof

\sketch There is one singular simplex in every dimension and the boundary maps alternate between an isomorphism and zero.

□

For nonempty $X$, reduced homology $\widetilde H_n(X)$ is the homology of \[ \cdots \to C_1(X)\xrightarrow {\partial }C_0(X)\xrightarrow {\varepsilon }\mathbb {Z}\to 0. \] Thus $H_0(X)\cong \widetilde H_0(X)\oplus \mathbb {Z}$ and $H_n(X)\cong \widetilde H_n(X)$ for $n>0$.
